sentence: This project studies how immune cells called macrophages and dendritic cells behave in the belly cavity as cancer spreads there and is treated.
This project studies how certain proteins in the cells lining the airway control how influenza A virus grows and causes inflammation in the lung.
This project teaches cancer researchers how to use qualitative research methods to explore the experiences of patients and providers.
This project studies how alcohol exposure early in development affects a brain circuit that controls working memory and decision making.
This project tries to make better versions of an antibiotic that acts on drug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria without harming the gut microbiome.
This project studies how radiation interacts with cancer and normal tissues and how imaging can guide cancer care.
This project studies how a protein called menin is broken down in acute leukemia and tries to build drugs that remove it.
This project builds AI tools and lab tests to find and interpret DNA changes outside genes that cause rare genetic diseases.
This project uses chemical approaches to probe basic biological mechanisms.
This project works with elementary schools to find out what affects children's bathroom use and tests a behavioral program to improve bladder symptoms.
This project studies how a viral protein helps hepatitis E virus leave liver cells, using cell culture and a rat model.
This project studies how cell adhesion and signaling between tissue layers guide the closing of the palate during fetal development.
This project tests whether video tools help parents of children with cancer make decisions about life-prolonging treatments.
This project uses electronic health record data and informatics methods to study how speaking two languages affects thinking skills in aging and dementia.
This project develops imaging tools and targeted agents to study cancer biology and to help diagnose and monitor cancer.
This project studies how microbes in the gut affect the immune response to a cholera vaccine.
This project tries to find which damaged DNA pieces called DNA adducts cause the unexplained mutation patterns seen in cancer genomes.
This project studies how simian arteriviruses enter cells, avoid the immune system, and could spread to humans.
This project studies how a long non-coding RNA called Xist changes T cell activation and contributes to autoimmunity in females.
This project interviews female Veterans and follows a large group over time to find which experiences predict suicide attempts.
